profiles.note: Device-class buckets (role × vendor). Attach Metric sets here; nodes inherit them via their profile.
profiles.unavailable: Profile management is unavailable in skeleton mode (no metadata store).

empty.noneSub: Add a device-class profile (e.g. “Cisco Catalyst switch”).

modal.pollIntervalPlaceholder: leave blank to use the system default
modal.pollIntervalHint: Overrides the system default for nodes using this profile. 10–3600 seconds; leave blank to inherit the default.

delete.confirm: Delete profile {{name}}? Nodes using it keep running but lose this class's collection defaults.

templates.empty: No metric sets exist yet. Create some first.
templates.gap_one: {{count}} metric collected here has an alert rule on other profiles but none on this one
templates.gap_other: {{count}} metrics collected here have alert rules on other profiles but none on this one
templates.gapHint: A default rule names the profiles it was written for, and this profile is not one of them — so these are collected and nothing can fire on them.
templates.covered_one: 1 metric collected here has an alert rule. The rest are raw values no rule bounds anywhere.
templates.covered_other: {{count}} metrics collected here have an alert rule. The rest are raw values no rule bounds anywhere.
templates.unchecked: Couldn't check which of these metrics have an alert rule — the rule list came back capped or unavailable.

err.pollInterval: Poll interval must be a whole number of seconds between 10 and 3600.

rules.note: Map a discovered device's sysObjectID / sysDescr to a Device profile. Discovery pre-selects the match on import.
rules.unavailable: Classification-rule management is unavailable in skeleton mode (no metadata store).

empty.noneSub: Add a rule mapping a sysObjectID prefix or sysDescr pattern to a profile.

modal.oidPrefixHint: Authoritative — outranks sysDescr. End with a dot so 1.3…9. won't also match …91. Pair with a sysDescr regex to split one vendor by NOS.
modal.descrRegexHintBoth: With a prefix set, both must match (vendor + NOS); on its own, it matches sysDescr directly.
modal.matcherRequired: Provide a sysObjectID prefix and/or a sysDescr regex.

delete.confirm: Delete the rule mapping {{sig}} → {{profile}}? Discovery will stop suggesting this profile for matching devices (already-imported nodes are unaffected).

reclassify.note: Nodes whose profile differs from the one the current classification rules choose. Nothing changes until you apply it.
reclassify.unavailable: Reclassification is unavailable in skeleton mode (no metadata store).
reclassify.empty: Every identified node already has the profile its rules choose.
reclassify.emptyUnidentified: No node has been identified yet ({{count}} waiting). For a node polled over SNMP, the poller reads what the device is within the hour.
reclassify.lockedHint: A locked node keeps its profile and is not listed; unlock it from the node's Edit dialog.
reclassify.unidentifiedHint: The poller reads what each device is on its hourly SNMP identity probe, so a node that is not polled over SNMP is never identified.

confirm.body: Their metric sets, profile thresholds and maintenance windows will follow the new profile.
confirm.stops: Metrics that only the old profile collected will stop.

result.applied: Applied to {{applied}}. Not applied: {{changed}} changed since this page loaded, {{locked}} locked, {{hidden}} not visible to you.

duplicates.note: Device nodes that look like the same device added more than once — at one address, or at two. Nothing is deleted until you choose.
duplicates.unavailable: Duplicate detection is unavailable in skeleton mode (no metadata store).
duplicates.counts: {{total}} groups ({{confident}} likely, {{possible}} to check) · {{scanned}} nodes compared
duplicates.truncated: Showing the first {{shown}} of {{total}} groups. Delete some and reload to see the rest.
duplicates.selectKeepers: Select all but the suggested keepers
duplicates.ignored_one: {{count}} value was not used as evidence because more than 8 nodes share it: {{values}}
duplicates.ignored_other: {{count}} values were not used as evidence because more than 8 nodes share each of them: {{values}}

block.keepOne: Every node of group {{groups}} is selected. Leave at least one node of each group.
block.tooMany: Select at most {{max}} nodes at a time.

duplicates.empty: No duplicates among the nodes you can see.
duplicates.emptyNothingToCompare: There are fewer than two device nodes to compare.
duplicates.emptyNoEvidence: No duplicates by address or name. None of the {{count}} nodes has a serial number or an address list yet; the poller reads both over SNMP once an hour, so look again later.
duplicates.hint: A likely duplicate shares an address, a serial number, a MAC address or an LLDP chassis ID, or each node lists the other's address. A group to check shares only weaker signs, or has something that disagrees. Two routers sharing a VRRP or HSRP address can show up as one device: keep both.

sets.note: Reusable metric bundles. Attach them to device profiles; editing one updates every profile that uses it.
sets.unavailable: Metric sets are unavailable in skeleton mode (no metadata store).

empty.noneSub: Add a reusable metric bundle (e.g. “Standard interfaces”).

delete.confirm: Delete metric set {{name}}? Profiles that attach it lose this bundle's metrics.

editor.pickerSearchPlaceholder: Search the MIB catalog by name / OID / vendor…
editor.emptyTemplate: No metrics in this set yet.
editor.emptyNode: No node-level metrics. The profile's metric sets / built-in defaults still apply.

mib.note: A curated OID catalog. Pick metrics by name in the collection editor instead of typing OIDs.
mib.unavailable: The MIB catalog is unavailable in skeleton mode.

modal.vendorHint: Leave blank for a standard (non-vendor) OID.

delete.confirm: Delete catalog entry {{name}}? Collections referencing it by name will no longer resolve from the catalog. This cannot be undone.

discovery.note: Find devices to monitor: sweep an address range, or review the devices your monitored equipment has already seen.

scans.title: Recent sweeps
scans.note: Sweeps this core is holding. Pick one to see its progress or its results.
scans.resumed: Showing a sweep that was already running.
scans.unknownScan: This core does not know that sweep — it restarted, or the sweep aged out. A poller may still be running it.
scans.pollFailed: Stopped checking this sweep after repeated errors. Reload to try again.
scans.queuedNote: Waiting for a poller to pick this sweep up. Nothing has been probed yet.
scans.stopRequested: Stop requested. The poller finishes what it is already probing, so this takes a few seconds.
scans.stopUnsupported: Stop requested, but a poller that could be running this sweep is too old to act on it — the sweep may run to completion.
scans.stoppedNote: Sweep stopped. The devices found before it stopped are below and can be imported.
scans.finishedAnyway: The sweep finished before the stop reached the poller.

site.label: Sweep a site
site.hint: Lists the ranges recorded for that site so you can pick which to sweep, and files anything you import into its folder.
site.overLimit: {{count}} addresses — more than the {{max}} one sweep can carry. Clear a range or two.

cannot.v6: IPv6 — a sweep tries every address in a range, and this one has far too many
cannot.tooLarge: too wide for one sweep (limit {{max}} addresses)

err.nothingTicked: Select at least one range to sweep.

pool.label: Sweep from
pool.anyHint: With no site chosen the sweep goes to whichever poller answers first — which may be one that cannot reach these addresses.
pool.deadHint: No live poller serves this site, so the sweep will go to whichever poller answers first instead.
pool.oneOf: One live poller in this site will run it.

seen.title: Seen on the network
seen.note: Devices your monitored equipment has seen that Yagra is not monitoring yet: hosts in a router’s ARP / IPv6 neighbor cache, LLDP and CDP neighbors that advertise a management address, OSPF neighbors and BGP peers, and senders of syslog or SNMP traps that no node claimed. No scan is needed. Phones and end stations behind a switch are left out of the LLDP / CDP half.

coverage.off: The ARP cache walk is off, so this list comes only from LLDP / CDP neighbors, routing peers and syslog / trap senders. Turn on the ARP / IPv6 neighbor cache walk under Settings ▸ System settings ▸ Discovery walks to add every host your routers have spoken to.
coverage.complete: ARP: {{nodes}} device(s) reporting, {{observed}} address(es) resolved in total.
coverage.sampled: ARP: {{nodes}} device(s) reporting, {{observed}} address(es) resolved — but {{truncated}} of them hit the row budget, so the ARP half of this list is a sample of what is out there, not all of it.

detect.hint: Try your SNMP credentials on this device and pick a profile from what it answers
detect.silent: No credential got an answer. Pick them by hand, or monitor by ping only.
detect.lost: The detection ended before it finished. Try again.
detect.idle: Tries the {{count}} credentials above and picks a profile from the answer.
detect.trying: Trying your SNMP credentials ({{count}}), about 2 s each.
detect.noCreds: No credential chosen above — Detect would only ping.
detect.credsHint: Detect tries these in this order — the same list as Scan a range, so a change here is a change there. <lnk>Manage credentials →</lnk>

err.import: failed to start monitoring that endpoint

seen.senderOnly: Only a syslog or trap sender vouches for this address, and a sender's address can be forged — so it is not detected or monitored from here. If it is yours, add it with Add node.

more.loaded: {{loaded}} of {{total}} unregistered devices loaded. Filters search only the loaded rows.

icmpGate.label: Also try SNMP where ping is blocked
icmpGate.hint: Off: an address that does not answer ping is skipped instead of being tried with every credential, which is what keeps a large range quick. Turn it on to find devices that block ICMP but answer SNMP.

discovery.signIn: Sign in as an admin to run discovery.
discovery.credsLink: Discovery uses your stored credentials. <lnk>Manage credentials →</lnk>

existing.outsideScope: Monitored in a folder you can't see

msg.imported_one: Imported {{count}} node — they will start polling shortly.
msg.imported_other: Imported {{count}} nodes — they will start polling shortly.
msg.importedInto_one: Imported {{count}} node into {{site}} — it will start polling shortly.
msg.importedInto_other: Imported {{count}} nodes into {{site}} — they will start polling shortly.
msg.importedFiled_one: Imported {{count}} node, {{filed}} filed by IP range.
msg.importedFiled_other: Imported {{count}} nodes, {{filed}} filed by IP range.
msg.contested_one: {{count}} of those is claimed by two folders.
msg.contested_other: {{count}} of those are claimed by two folders.
msg.skippedExisting_one: Skipped {{count}} device already in the tree.
msg.skippedExisting_other: Skipped {{count}} devices already in the tree.

err.badTargets: Enter IPs, CIDRs (≤/20), or ranges (e.g. 192.168.1.10-20), comma-separated — ≤4096 hosts total.
err.selectOne: Select at least one device to import.

fileByPrefix.label: File each device by its IP range
fileByPrefix.hint: Each device goes into the folder whose IP range contains its address. One that no range covers — or that two folders claim equally well — goes into the folder chosen above instead.

why.noRanges: no folder has an IP range yet
